messages.author: 13d01984f5682713
messages.subject: truncated normal distribution in rstan
parts:
In my model, one prior is truncated  N(0,100), the parameter should be greater than 0, so the prior in the model block should be 
beta~normal(0,100)T[0,].
Can anyone tell me if this is right. Any help is appreciated.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] truncated normal distribution in rstan
parts:
That's incorrect.

In the parameter's block, declare beta as:
  real<lower = 0> beta;

In the model block, you can now use:
  beta ~ normal(0, 100);

If you really wanted to, you could use:
  beta ~ normal(0, 100) T[0, ];
but that's going to compute the normalizing constant, which isn't needed.



Daniel
